flows.name: Workbench
flows.description: Someone opens the workbench, starts an antenna (from a template, a blank board they draw on, or an imported Gerber, DXF or STEP file), solves it and reads the results.
flows.provenance: Screens captured on Nov 21, 2026 from main at ac0d27d plus the fixes in this branch, in headless Chromium with SwiftShader WebGPU at 1440×900. SwiftShader is a software GPU, so the solve on screen takes 4 minutes; a laptop GPU solves the same example in a few seconds.

nodes.title: Open the workbench
nodes.summary: The default example, an inset-fed patch for the 5.8 GHz band, opens ready to solve. The status line says "Ready to solve"; result tabs stay off until a solve lands (a click on one says why).

nodes.title: Restored last session
nodes.summary: A reload brings back the last project, unsaved edits included, and says so. Open an example to start over.

nodes.title: Saved copy unreadable
nodes.summary: A saved copy that no longer loads is reported and the example opens instead, without asking to keep the broken copy.

nodes.title: New project
nodes.summary: Four starting points: patch, microstrip line, differential pair, or a blank board. Frequency, laminate and thickness size the template; the board size can be left to the template.

nodes.title: Blank board
nodes.summary: Ground, laminate and an empty top layer. The panel says the project cannot be solved yet because it has no port; the message line says what to do next.

nodes.title: Drew a patch, feed and port
nodes.summary: Rectangle and Port tools in the top view. Edges now line up with nearby copper, so the feed meets the patch exactly.
nodes.finding: Fixed in this branch: points snapped only to the 0.1 mm grid, so a hand-drawn feed ended 0.1 mm short of the patch. See 4c for what that cost.

nodes.title: Imported Gerber copper and outline
nodes.summary: KiCad front copper onto layer top, then the Edge_Cuts file as the board outline, both with the file coordinates kept.

nodes.title: STEP: choose the bodies
nodes.summary: After choosing a STEP file, the dialog lists its bodies by height with the selector that picks each group.
nodes.finding: Fixed in this branch: the dialog asked for body names ("*_PCB") without showing any, so a first-time user had to guess. The list only appeared in an error.

nodes.title: Wrong kind of file
nodes.summary: A project file chosen in Import is refused with a plain message pointing to Open.
nodes.finding: Fixed in this branch: any file that was not DXF or STEP was parsed as Gerber, and a JSON file failed with "command … is not terminated by *".

nodes.title: Copper off the board
nodes.summary: STEP copper kept at KiCad page coordinates (x 80 to 98 mm) lands outside a new 62 mm board. A warning now says a solve would leave it out and how to fix it.
nodes.finding: Fixed in this branch: the import reported success and the copper silently fell outside the board; only the mesh warning at solve time mentioned it.

nodes.title: Unsaved changes
nodes.summary: New, Open, an example or a dropped file over an edited project asks first: "Open … ? Your unsaved changes to … will be lost." Cancel keeps everything.

nodes.title: Patch from the template
nodes.summary: A 2.45 GHz edge-fed patch on FR-4, sized from the textbook formulas, ready to solve.

nodes.title: Value does not parse
nodes.summary: "banana mm" in a variable. The field says why, the tree marks the variable, Solve is disabled, and the model keeps the last valid version.

nodes.title: Port off copper
nodes.summary: Moving the feed port off the trace turns the status amber and the message names the port and layer. Solve stays enabled; that port would drive nothing.

nodes.title: Solving
nodes.summary: The button turns to Stop. The progress bar shows the step and how far the energy has fallen; the message line gives the grid size and step limit.

nodes.title: Stopped
nodes.summary: Stop ends the worker at once. Nothing partial is shown; the earlier result, if any, stays.

nodes.title: No WebGPU: CPU fallback
nodes.summary: Without a WebGPU adapter the solve runs on the CPU, with a warning that it is much slower and how to get the GPU.

nodes.title: Hand-drawn gap: 0.1 mm cell
nodes.summary: The drawn feed and patch were 0.1 mm apart. The mesh put lines there, that cell set the time step, and the solve hit its 40,000-step budget. Still running after 6 minutes on SwiftShader.
nodes.finding: Fixed at the source in this branch (draw snapping, 2b). The warning text is still written for a mesh expert: it names edge_cell but not which two edges are close.

nodes.title: Reloaded mid-solve
nodes.summary: Leaving during a solve asks first. After a reload or crash the page says the solve did not finish and nothing was kept.

nodes.title: GPU device lost
nodes.summary: A driver reset ends the solve with a message that suggests solving again or CPU only, instead of hanging.

nodes.title: S-parameters
nodes.summary: S11 with the deepest dip, the −10 dB bandwidth, solver, mesh and steps beside it. Touchstone, CSV and image export.

nodes.title: Smith chart
nodes.summary: The same S11 on a Smith chart, with the −10 dB circle.

nodes.title: Impedance
nodes.summary: Input impedance over the band, Z at the design frequency.

nodes.title: Edited after the solve
nodes.summary: Any edit marks the results as from the earlier version. Undo back to the solved document clears it.

nodes.title: Fields on the model
nodes.summary: Surface current on the copper at 5.8 GHz, with a legend and image export. Ez plays through a cycle; Video records it.

nodes.title: Radiation lobe
nodes.summary: The 3D gain pattern over the board.

nodes.title: Cut mode needs another solve
nodes.summary: Cuts record E and H in the whole box, so only a solve started in Cut mode has them. "Solve with cuts" starts one.
nodes.finding: Fixed in this branch: while a solve was running, "Solve with cuts" called solve(), which stopped it. It is now disabled while anything runs.

nodes.title: Video during a solve
nodes.summary: Video now refuses to start while a solve runs, and a file dropped during encoding is not opened.
nodes.finding: Fixed in this branch: recording held the Stop button, so a running solve could not be stopped, and its result replaced the field mid-recording.

nodes.title: Far field
nodes.summary: E- and H-plane cuts with directivity, gain, realized gain, efficiency, beamwidth, front to back and cross-polar.
nodes.finding: The polar plots fill about a third of the panel and their labels are small at 1440×900 (open since Nov 19).

nodes.title: Emissions
nodes.summary: Near-field scan above the board and the field at 3 m and 10 m against reference limits.

nodes.title: Rank variables
nodes.summary: Which variables move the result most: two solves per unlocked variable. Not run in this walkthrough (each solve takes minutes on SwiftShader).

flows.name: Solve engine
flows.description: What one workbench solve goes through behind the progress bar, from meshing to the far field, and every way it can end early. Each state shows the message the page prints.
flows.provenance: Messages copied from src/workbench/solve.ts, main.ts and src/engine/energy_stop.ts at ac0d27d. The grid, steps and times come from the SwiftShader walkthrough run; the numbers in the failure messages are examples.

nodes.title: Building the mesh
nodes.log: Building the mesh
nodes.summary: The project is rasterised onto the graded mesh in the worker. Mesh warnings are printed before the time loop starts.

nodes.title: Project cannot be meshed
nodes.log: The solve failed: $.vias[0] via at (31.2, 0) mm reaches off the board
nodes.summary: A rasterise error ends the solve before any GPU work, for example a via that runs off the board.

nodes.title: A tiny cell
nodes.log: Warning  mesh: smallest cell 0.100 mm is below edge_cell (0.35 mm) and sets the time step; look for copper edges, the port or layer interfaces closer together than edge_cell.
nodes.summary: Two edges a hair apart set a small cell, and the smallest cell sets the time step for the whole grid.
nodes.finding: The text is for a mesh expert. It should name the two edges (shape ids and coordinates) that are close.

nodes.title: GPU setup
nodes.log: Info  Solving on WebGPU: 85 × 79 × 45 cells (0.30 million), up to 20,000 steps.
nodes.summary: Buffers for the grid are allocated and the shaders compiled.

nodes.title: No WebGPU adapter
nodes.log: Warning  This browser has no WebGPU adapter, so the solve runs on the CPU, which is much slower. Chrome or Edge with hardware acceleration on uses the GPU.
nodes.summary: The CPU solver runs instead, with a warning. "CPU only" picks it on purpose.

nodes.title: WebGPU setup failed
nodes.log: The solve failed: WebGPU setup failed for this 85 × 79 × 45 grid: … Choose "CPU only" to solve it on the processor.
nodes.summary: The grid does not fit the GPU, or a buffer is refused. No silent fallback.

nodes.title: Time loop
nodes.log:
step 6,500
energy down 41 of 50 dB · 3:28
nodes.summary: Steps run in batches. Every check, the field energy is compared with its peak; the run stops once it has fallen by the amount asked for.

nodes.title: Stopped
nodes.log: Info  Solve stopped.
nodes.summary: The worker is terminated; there is no stopping state.

nodes.title: GPU device lost
nodes.log: The solve failed: The GPU stopped during the solve (…). Drivers do this when a GPU job runs too long or the laptop switches graphics cards. Solve again, or choose "CPU only".
nodes.summary: Every GPU wait races device.lost, so a driver reset ends the solve.

nodes.title: No field at all
nodes.log: The solve failed: The field energy is still zero after 812 steps, with the source finished: the solver produced no fields. On the GPU this usually means the device ran out of memory or rejected a buffer; try a coarser mesh or "CPU only".
nodes.summary: Energy still zero after the source ended: on the GPU this is almost always out of memory. Before #76 this showed a flat 0 dB "converged" result.

nodes.title: Diverged
nodes.log: The solve failed: The field energy became NaN after 2400 steps: the solve diverged. Check for a cell far smaller than its neighbors or a material constant that is not physical.
nodes.summary: A non-finite energy ends the run.
nodes.finding: Fixed in this branch: UK spelling ("neighbours") in a message the user reads.

nodes.title: Step limit first
nodes.log: Warning  The field fell 31.0 dB of the 50 dB asked for within 40000 steps, so the results are approximate. Raise analysis.stop.max_steps.
nodes.summary: The run hits max_steps before the energy falls far enough. Results are shown, marked approximate.

nodes.title: Fields and far field
nodes.log: Computing the far field
nodes.summary: The DFT planes are read back and the near-to-far transform runs.

nodes.title: Gain approximate
nodes.log: Warning  The run stopped before the field rang down, so efficiency and gain are approximate. The pattern shape is less affected.
nodes.summary: With the field not rung down, efficiency and gain are approximate; the pattern shape much less so.

nodes.title: Solved
nodes.log: Info  Solved in 4:03.6 on WebGPU, google swiftshader (time loop 4:00.9).
nodes.summary: The result replaces the last one and the S-parameters tab opens.

nodes.title: Page closed mid-solve
nodes.log: Warning  The solve of patch-5g8-far-field.json started at 14:58 did not finish: the page was reloaded, closed or crashed. Nothing from it was kept. The project is unchanged, so Solve runs it again.
nodes.summary: The running solve is kept in sessionStorage; finding it at the next start means it never finished.

flows.name: Sentence race (one lane)
flows.description: npm run design -- agent-race "<sentence>": the same sentence goes to Kimi on Cerebras and on a GPU provider, each driving NobuRF through OpenClaw behind a spend-guarded proxy. This map follows one lane; the second lane is held until the first finishes.
flows.provenance: From PR #57 (branch claude/project-thread-6l7qqu at 033d1d1, not on main yet): scripts/design.ts, src/design/openclaw_lane.ts and model_proxy.ts. The lane runs in a terminal, so each state shows a terminal line. The line formats come from the code; the sentence, numbers and error wording inside them are examples, since no real-model run was captured for this map.

nodes.title: Sentence in
nodes.log:
$ npm run design -- agent-race "a 2.4 GHz patch under 30 mm, S11 at most -10 dB"
kimi on cerebras via OpenClaw, medium effort: spent so far $0.4120 of the $4 cap; run cap $1
nodes.summary: Both lane keys are checked, the spend ledger is read, and the run folders are created under runs/agent/race-<time>.

nodes.title: A key is missing
nodes.log: Error: CEREBRAS_API_KEY is not set (environment or .env): lane cerebras cannot run
nodes.summary: The race refuses to start rather than run one lane.

nodes.title: Harnesses start
nodes.log: (OpenClaw loading, starting the NobuRF MCP server; 4 to 9 minutes on the Windows laptop)
nodes.summary: Both OpenClaw harnesses start at once, each with its own state folder and no keys in its environment. Each holds its first model request at the proxy.

nodes.title: No request in 900 s
nodes.log: cerebras: OpenClaw sent no model request within 900 s; ending the lane
nodes.summary: A harness that never asks for a model turn is killed, so the race cannot hang on it.

nodes.title: Second lane held
nodes.log: (second lane: first request held at the proxy)
nodes.summary: The second lane is up but waits at the proxy until the first lane ends; the lanes never share the solver.

nodes.title: Race starts
nodes.log: both harnesses are up: the race starts
nodes.summary: Once both harnesses are up, the first lane's request goes through and its clock starts. Start-up time is reported apart from the race.

nodes.title: Spend cap
nodes.log: [cerebras] model call 402: run cap $1 would be passed
nodes.summary: Before each call the proxy reserves its worst-case cost; a call that would pass the run or provider cap gets 402 and is never sent.

nodes.title: Rate limited
nodes.log:
[openrouter] model call 429: rate limited
...
wall 212 s = model 140 s + tools 51 s + rate-limit waits 21 s
nodes.summary: A 429 is passed back to OpenClaw, which waits and retries. The wait is counted apart from thinking time.

nodes.title: Agent designs
nodes.log:
[cerebras] model 1.8 s, 412 tokens: start_design {"target_ghz":2.4,...}
[cerebras] model 0.9 s, 120 tokens: solve {}
nodes.summary: start_design reads the sentence into a goal, then the agent solves, edits and optimizes through the NobuRF tools.

nodes.title: Person types a correction
nodes.log:
type a message and press Enter to tell the agent something while it works
> make it 2.45 GHz
nodes.summary: A line typed in the terminal goes to the session inbox and reaches the model with the next tool result.

nodes.title: Deadline
nodes.log: harness_error: best confirmed null
nodes.summary: A harness still running at its timeout plus 60 s is killed (the whole process tree on Windows).

nodes.title: Finish
nodes.log: [cerebras] model 1.1 s, 88 tokens: finish {"summary":"..."}
nodes.summary: The agent calls finish. The proxy closes and the calls are written to model-calls.json.

nodes.title: Ended without finish
nodes.log: no_finish: best confirmed {"f0_ghz":2.41,...}
nodes.summary: OpenClaw exited cleanly but the agent never called finish; the summary says no_finish, or spend_cap if a call was refused.

nodes.title: Closing confirm
nodes.log: closing_confirm (6.2 s) -> {"met":true,...}
nodes.summary: After OpenClaw exits, the best design is solved once more at confirm fidelity, on the lane's clock.

nodes.title: Replay files
nodes.log:
cerebras: met, model 38.2 s, $0.21 -> runs/agent/race-…/cerebras.replay.json
play it: npm run design -- serve, then open http://localhost:8000/launch/race-replay/?left=…&right=…
nodes.summary: Both lanes done: replay logs and lobes are written and the command prints the replay link.

nodes.title: Lanes read it differently
nodes.log: warning: the lanes read the request differently ({"target_ghz":2.4} vs {"target_ghz":2.45}); the race view says so
nodes.summary: If the two models set different goals from the same sentence, the race says so on the replay.

flows.name: Bridge demo page (Nov 19)
flows.description: Someone opens NobuRF, sees the baseline patch antenna, edits the geometry and solves until S11 at 5.8 GHz drops below −10 dB.
flows.provenance: Screens captured on Nov 19, 2026 from commit 849c782 in headless Chromium with SwiftShader WebGPU. That is a software GPU, so solves read 38 to 58 s; on a GTX 1660 Ti the same solve takes 552 ms.

nodes.title: Open the app
nodes.summary: The page starts WebGPU, asks the bridge for the current design and solves it: 3,000 steps on a 64×64×48 grid. The panel stays empty until that first solve lands.

nodes.title: Bridge not running
nodes.summary: Without the bridge the page solves the baseline on its own and says “local mode”. The agent cannot reach this page.
nodes.finding: Apply and Reset still post to the bridge. Clicking Apply in local mode fails with “Unexpected end of JSON input”. Disable both and say the bridge is off.

nodes.title: No WebGPU
nodes.summary: No adapter means no solve. The status line reads “WebGPU unavailable: No WebGPU adapter found” and the panel stays empty.
nodes.finding: The message is small, in a corner, and gives no next step. Name the browsers that work and how to turn WebGPU on.

nodes.title: GPU device lost
nodes.summary: On Windows, Edge can pick the integrated GPU. A long GPU job trips the driver’s 2 s watchdog and the device is lost. Runs are now split into submits of 250 steps or fewer.
nodes.finding: If the device is lost anyway, it is only logged to the console. The status keeps saying “solving”.

nodes.title: Baseline result
nodes.summary: The edge-fed patch is badly matched: −2.4 dB at 5.8 GHz and a shallow dip at 5.40 GHz. Z_in is 11+j41 Ω, so the badge says mismatched.

nodes.title: Manual edit
nodes.summary: One geometry edit as JSON. Apply sends it through the bridge, so the page and the agent always work on the same design.

nodes.title: Typo in the edit
nodes.summary: A missing brace. The status line shows the raw parser message; the box keeps the text, so the fix is one keystroke.
nodes.finding: “Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 20 (line 1 column 21)” appears far from the box. Show it under the box, in plain words.

nodes.title: Value out of range
nodes.summary: The bridge answers 422 and the page shows “inset_depth_mm=40 out of range [0, 5.58]”. Nothing is solved and the design is unchanged.

nodes.title: Solving the edit
nodes.summary: The status line reads “solving #1…” while the old result stays on screen. Buttons are disabled until the bridge answers.

nodes.title: Solve slower than 15 s
nodes.summary: The bridge stops waiting after 15 s and returns 504, which is what this screen shows. The page keeps solving in the background.
nodes.finding: In a run on Nov 19 the late result still landed in the log as #1, although the bridge never committed the edit. The next edit was also #1, applied to the old design. Page and bridge disagree.

nodes.title: Dip found, off target
nodes.summary: A 4 mm inset pulls the dip down to −19.3 dB, but at 5.55 GHz. At 5.8 GHz the match is still −2.5 dB, so the badge stays red.

nodes.title: Matched
nodes.summary: Length 11 mm, inset 2 mm, width 20 mm: −16.7 dB at 5.8 GHz, with the dip at 5.85 GHz and 200 MHz of −10 dB bandwidth.

nodes.title: Edit below the grid
nodes.summary: 0.2 mm is finer than the 0.5 mm grid, so the geometry does not change. The cached result comes back and the log adds #3 with the same −16.7 dB.
nodes.finding: The agent gets a no_voxel_change warning. The page shows none, so a person sees a solve that did nothing. Show the warning in the log row.

nodes.title: Share view
nodes.summary: Adding ?share hides the edit box, status line and GPU chips, for clean screenshots and video.

nodes.title: Another tab took over
nodes.summary: Opening a second tab hands the bridge to it. The first tab stops answering and does not reconnect.
nodes.finding: It says “bridge offline · npm run dev”, but the bridge is running. Say another NobuRF tab is in control.

edges.label: No adapter
edges.condition: the browser has no WebGPU adapter

edges.label: Integrated GPU
edges.condition: a GPU job outlasts the driver watchdog

edges.label: 15 s passed
edges.condition: solve takes longer than BRIDGE_SOLVE_TIMEOUT_MS (15 s)

edges.label: Under 0.5 mm
edges.condition: edit voxelises to the same grid

edges.label: Second tab
edges.condition: bridge closes the old socket with code 4000

flows.name: Knob-tuning race (Nov 19)
flows.description: The same Kimi K3.1 Pro agent tunes the same antenna twice at once: one lane on Cerebras, one on a GPU provider. Only the host differs.
flows.provenance: Screens from the offline rehearsal (npm run race) on Nov 19, 2026, with a scripted model at simulated speeds and the analytic mock solver. Every time on this map comes from those simulated speeds. Race frames are site/race.html (commit 65bc89f) replaying that run.

nodes.title: Start the race
nodes.summary: One command starts the bridge, a timing proxy per provider and two OpenClaw agents. Live mode adds -- --mode live.

nodes.title: No solver tab
nodes.summary: With no NobuRF tab connected, the harness attaches the analytic mock solver. Its S11 comes from a transmission-line model, not a full-wave solve.

nodes.title: API key missing
nodes.summary: Live mode needs CEREBRAS_API_KEY and FIREWORKS_API_KEY in .env. Without one, the harness exits with code 2 before it starts anything.

nodes.title: Both agents ready
nodes.summary: Each proxy holds its lane’s first model call until both agents have booted, then starts both clocks at once. Start-up time stays off the race clock. The replay shows this moment as both clocks at 0.0.

nodes.title: Model thinks
nodes.summary: Same model, prompt, tools and reasoning effort in both lanes. The timing proxy records time to first token, tokens and decode speed per call.

nodes.title: Rate limited
nodes.summary: A test on Nov 19 got 429 request_quota_exceeded on the 6th request (free tier, gpt-oss-120b). The proxy passes the 429 to OpenClaw.
nodes.finding: Not tested in a race. Nobody knows yet whether OpenClaw retries or the lane ends as an error.

nodes.title: Spending cap reached
nodes.summary: Nothing stops a race on spend. The meter shows requests and tokens per minute against the hackathon limits (100 and 100K). rate_meter.ts has a waitForBudget, but nothing calls it.
nodes.finding: Add a token budget per race that finishes a lane as gave_up when it runs out.

nodes.title: Agent crashed
nodes.summary: If OpenClaw exits with an error mid-run, the lane is finished as error and the report keeps the first 300 characters of its message.

nodes.title: Edit and solve
nodes.summary: Each apply_edit runs a full solve and returns telemetry with a one-line reason the viewer sees. Both lanes share one GPU, so solves queue.

nodes.title: Edit rejected
nodes.summary: The model gets the bridge’s 422 message and a hint naming the fix. The lane keeps running.

nodes.title: Solve timed out
nodes.summary: After 15 s the bridge returns 504. The hint tells the model to retry once, then stop and report.

nodes.title: Solver offline
nodes.summary: No solver is connected, so the bridge returns 503. The hint tells the model to stop and ask for the NobuRF page to be opened.

nodes.title: Gave up
nodes.summary: The prompt caps a lane at 12 edits. The replay stamps the lane STOPPED in red, and the report lists it as gave_up.

nodes.title: First lane matches
nodes.summary: The Cerebras lane reaches −24.9 dB after two edits, at 2.8 s. The GPU lane is still on its first turn.

nodes.title: Both lanes finish
nodes.summary: The GPU lane matches at 16.3 s with the same two edits and the same −24.9 dB.

nodes.title: Report
nodes.summary: summary.md and race.json record race time, model time, tokens and decode speed per lane. Every model call is in events.jsonl.

edges.label: Key missing
edges.condition: --mode live runs without a key in .env
